q: This study aims to empirically investigate whether instructions documented in agent context files are reflected in agent-generated software artifacts.
r: Include: empirical study of agent context files and agent compliance across 6,541 agent commits (group b).

q: This paper studies whether a short value statement in an agent’s persistent instruction file changes not only how well the agent performs but also what it builds.
r: Include: controlled multi-run evaluation of an instruction-file value statement on a coding agent (group b).

q: We evaluate Spark as a coach for AI coding agents performing software development tasks.
r: Include: shared experiential memory layer for coding agents with code-quality evaluation (group b, borderline: DS-1000 snippet-level tasks).

q: Through a qualitative analysis of 401 open-source repositories with cursor rules, we developed a comprehensive taxonomy of project context that developers consider essential
r: Include: large-scale empirical study of Cursor rules files for AI coding assistants (group b).

q: we introduce OCTOBENCH, a repository-grounded benchmark for measuring instruction following under realistic agentic coding scaffolds.
r: Include: benchmark of coding-agent adherence to repository policy files, skills and system prompts (group b).

q: SWE-ContextBench contains 1,476 tasks from 51 unique GitHub repositories spanning 9 programming languages
r: Include: benchmark on memory/context reuse for coding agents with cost and runtime metrics (group b; tasks are SWE-Bench issue repair, which EC6 would exclude only under group c).

q: We present SKILLROUTER, a compact body-aware retrieve-and-rerank pipeline built from standard IR components
r: IC1: contribution is an information-retrieval skill router, not the use or evaluation of context mechanisms or coding agents on development tasks.

q: We seek to estimate the marginal effect of repository-derived code knowledge itself under fixed repository snapshot, fixed task, fixed model, fixed execution environment, and fixed evaluation metric.
r: Include: main contribution is an evaluation method (time-consistent matched A/B benchmark protocol for SWE agents), so EC6 (ii) holds.

q: Modern LLM-based coding agents support a skill mechanism that lets users extend agent behavior with pre-packaged instructions.
r: Include: optimisation of agent skills (instruction files) for coding agents with token cost and functional quality evaluation (group b).

q: Each method is run 10 times per task; a run passes only when its solution passes the full automated test suite, so pass rate is the fraction of passing runs.
r: Include: agent skills for SE tasks evaluated on pass rate and cost with 10 repetitions against a no-skill baseline (group b).
